I'm 52 and I've been working this 4.1 mu plot for 30 years. With seven people in the house and some of them working off-farm, I have to balance farm work with the cash they bring in. We rely on well irrigation here, so pumping costs are always on my mind.

This year I'll put 2.5 mu into stevia and 1.6 mu into cotton. Stevia has been good to us—the buyers pay about 6 yuan per kilogram and they come right to the village. Cotton prices are a bit soft, but I keep it as insurance. I can't put all my land into one crop.

For the stevia, I'll plant the chengguang improved variety. I buy 8,000 seedlings per mu from the seed dealer in town. In late March I'll do rotary tillage and lay down about 100 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as a base, plus another 80 kg per mu topdressing when the plants start vigorous growth. That gives me roughly 28 kg nitrogen per mu. I'll irrigate five times from the well—stevia is thirsty in June and July. I expect about 550 kg per mu if we don't get a bad drought. I'll spray pesticides about 9 times total, mostly insecticide and herbicide, with a little fungicide if the leaves start spotting.

For cotton, I'll plant guoxinmian hybrid seed in mid-April. I'll rotary till first and use plastic film to warm the soil. I'll put down 120 kg per mu of compound fertilizer and topdress with about 20 kg of urea when it flowers. That works out to roughly 25 kg of nitrogen per mu. I'll irrigate three times—at planting, flowering, and boll stage. Cotton needs more pesticide than stevia; I'll spray about 12 times to keep the bollworms and aphids off. I expect around 520 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I know some farmers apply more fertilizer, but with only 4.1 mu I have to watch every yuan. My neighbor applied 40 kg nitrogen per mu last year and only got 50 kg more yield—hardly worth the extra cost. I'd rather save that money for my grandson's school fees.
